text: For a 500x220 nm silicon strip waveguide the resonance sensitivity is roughly delta-lambda = 0.55*delta-w + 1.8*delta-t (nm shift per nm of width/thickness error). What design doctrine does this force on photonic computing architectures?
choices: No photonic computing architecture may assume as-drawn dimensions; tuning, calibration, and their power budgets are architectural constants
Rings should be made as small as possible to reduce sensitivity
Thickness errors matter less than width errors
Fabrication scatter is negligible because 2-5 nm errors are small
explanation: Because routine 2-5 nm dimensional scatter displaces ring resonances by tens of linewidths, no design can trust as-drawn dimensions; tuning and calibration power (tens of mW per ring, watts per weight bank) must be budgeted up front. Choice 1 misunderstands the per-nm index sensitivity; choice 2 is backwards (the 1.8 thickness coefficient exceeds the 0.55 width coefficient); choice 3 ignores that nm errors still dwarf pm-scale linewidths.
